speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my office. I understand you are experiencing occasional shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings after your tympanoplasty. To help me understand what is happening, can you tell me how much time has passed since your surgery?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Granuloma (Meatogranuloma) secondary to tympanoplasty graft failure or persistent middle ear pathology. The combination of shooting ear pain while eating (suggesting Eustachian tube involvement) and tenderness to earrings (suggesting canal inflammation or granulation tissue) 12 weeks post-op in a patient with a history of chronic otitis media is highly suspicious for this condition. I recommend an otoscopic examination with microscopic visualization of the tympanic membrane and canal.
